Accelerates biomolecular structure prediction inference for models like OpenFold3 and Boltz-2 on NVIDIA H100 and H200 GPUs.

By optimizing discovery-scale workloads, BioIR reduces the energy required to generate 31 million protein complex predictions for the AlphaFold Database by an estimated 1.35 GWh - the equivalent of 18,000 EV charges or 5.4 million electric vehicle miles.

items.title: WARNING: AI Agents Are Breaking Into Enterprise Systems and No One Knows Who Is Responsible
items.summary:
In 2019, Reliance acquired Reverie Language Technologies, a language tech pioneer built on just over $4 million in funding by Vivekanand Pani, Arvind Pani, and S. K. Mohanty. Rather than stepping away after the exit, the founding team reunited to establish Coremantle to solve a deeper systemic challenge exposed by their earlier work: the severe scarcity of high-quality Indic language training data. With 22 official languages, hundreds of regional dialects, code-switching, and domain-specific vocabularies, every Indic language expands into thousands of distinct data engineering problems.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Vivekanand Pani, Co-Founder of Coremantle, to unpack 30 years of Indic language computing. They discuss the historical evolution from 1990s desktop localization to modern speech models, the limitations of synthetic data generation for low-resource languages, why word error rates jump sixfold in real-world conversational field tests, commoditizing AI models, and building authentic, natural datasets for sovereign Indic AI.

Can natural, field-sourced Indic data bridge the gap between benchmark claims and real-world enterprise utility?

items.title: Inside Chariot: Parth Sarthi on Building Native Speech-Reasoning AI for India
items.summary:
While global frontier labs chase multi-trillion-parameter text models requiring gigawatt data centers, Indian AI startup Chariot is betting on an efficient 8-billion-parameter architecture natively engineered for speech reasoning. Co-founded by Suvrat Bhooshan (Gan.ai) and Parth Sarthi (ex-Stanford, DeepMind, Contextual AI), Chariot was selected under the India AI Mission to build sovereign voice AI. Rather than chaining together separate ASR, text LLM, and TTS models, Chariot's end-to-end speech-native architecture reasons directly in audio, eliminating translation latency and preserving pitch, emphasis, and emotional context across Indic dialects.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Parth Sarthi, Co-Founder of Chariot, to explore the future of speech-native foundation models. They discuss building beyond 22 official Indic languages into regional dialects, overcoming cross-lingual modality gaps, navigating India AI Mission GPU allocations, evaluating tokens per watt in inference workloads, and proving that surgical, domain-focused architectures can outcompete generalized text APIs.

Can end-to-end speech-reasoning models unlock the next generation of voice-first AI across the Global South?
